texts: Hesper skims each cauldron at sundown.
Hesper lifts the slick into prewarmed clay vessels with a broad ladle.
Each cauldron yields a partial vessel of mire-essence.
Good threads yield a full vessel.
Poor threads yield a thin slick.
Hesper dates and labels each vessel.
Hesper carries the vessels to the cellars.
The cellar shelves are arranged by year and month.
The old vessels stand at the front of the shelves.

fields.sentence: Hesper skims each cauldron at sundown.

review.notes: The explicit universal 'each cauldron' correctly ranges over (Member $x cauldron) with strength 1.0/0.9 and its QuantifierPhrase companion, and the constant agent plus the Time term sit inside the consequent as required. No (Every e 1 day) is added for the habitual 'at sundown', which is right since the frequency machinery keys on periodic wording ('every …'), not on a bare day-part adjunct.

fields.sentence: Hesper lifts the slick into prewarmed clay vessels with a broad ladle.

q1_issues.issue: "prewarmed" is fused into the kind symbol `prewarmed_clay_vessel`, but the compound rule bars fusing an incidental-description adjective ("a dented pail" is two atoms, not `dented_pail`) — a participle used as a modifier is an adjective, and a pre-warmed state is incidental description, so the licensed symbol is `clay_vessel` with `prewarmed` predicated separately.
`(Inheritance prewarmed_clay_vessel prewarmed)` exposes a modifier that is outside the closed gradable / positional-cardinal / material-adjective list the modifier-genus rule licenses.

q2_gaps: a bare-plural NP filling a motion oblique (`Goal` "into prewarmed clay vessels") in a non-episodic habitual clause: the group-witness-vs-bare-kind-filler rule is stated only for a bare-plural **direct object** in an **episodic** clause, so nothing decides between a `GroupOf` witness and the bare kind constant used here
review.notes: The motion-result routing is exactly right — `Theme` for the displaced slick, `Goal` for the "into" path, no `Result` atom — as are the `Instrument` with-phrase and the untensed habitual present. The same parse splits "a broad ladle" correctly into `(Member sk_ladle_1 ladle) (Member sk_ladle_1 broad)`, which is the treatment "prewarmed" should have received.

issues.reason: 'Prewarmed' is a participial modifier — an adjective by the instruction set's own ruling — and a transient prepared state is incidental description, which the fusion rule bars ('a dented pail' is two atoms) and which its participle example predicates separately ('a laminated worktop' -> `(Member sk_worktop_1 laminated)`), so only the classifier `clay_vessel` may fuse.

The modifier-genus rule's operative criterion is its stated predication test — 'can the modifier be predicated of the thing', with the line drawn as 'part of speech, not meaning' — and `prewarmed` is an adjective predicable of the vessel, so exposure is licensed; the three named cases illustrate 'an adjectival property of the referent' rather than closing the list.

gaps_confirmed: a bare-plural NP filling an oblique of a HABITUAL/generic clause: the group-witness rule is stated for a bare plural in an EPISODIC clause, and a group witness here would individuate one specific set of vessels across all occasions, while the bare-kind filler the parse chose has no slot to carry a distributed descriptive modifier
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form fuses only the classifier — `clay_vessel`, genus `(Inheritance clay_vessel vessel)`, `clay` unexposed as a noun modifier — and predicates `prewarmed` separately of the referent, which for a plural is the stated split (a fusing classifier rides the group's kind slot, a descriptive modifier distributes over the members as `(Implication (PartOf $x <group>) (Member $x prewarmed))`), exactly the treatment this same parse gave 'a broad ladle'.
adjudication.notes: The motion-result routing (`Theme` for the displaced slick, `Goal` for the 'into' path, no `Result` atom), the `Instrument` with-phrase, and the untensed habitual present are all correct. The group witness the compliant form needs sits uneasily with the habitual reading, which is the residual gap recorded above.

fields.sentence: Each cauldron yields a partial vessel of mire-essence.
parse: (: cauldron_yield_rule (Implication (Member $x cauldron) (And (Member (sk_yield $x) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $x) $x) (Patient (sk_yield $x) (sk_vessel $x)) (Member (sk_vessel $x) vessel) (Member (sk_vessel $x) partial) (Of (sk_vessel $x) mire_essence))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: a CONTAINER / MEASURE of-phrase over a mass noun ('a partial vessel of mire-essence', the instruction set's own 'a cup of water'): the of-phrase section explicitly excludes it from the genitive Possession route but supplies no positive encoding anywhere, so the container-quantity reading has no licensed form

an adjective modifying such a container quantity ('a PARTIAL vessel of X' = a partial vesselful): the ordinary adjective rule puts the property on the container object itself, which says the vessel is incomplete rather than that it holds a part-measure; no rule addresses the quantity reading
review.notes: The explicit universal correctly becomes a distributing rule at 1.0/0.9 with its mandatory QuantifierPhrase companion, the dependent existential is a Skolem function of $x per the forall-exists pattern, and 'mire-essence' decomposes once to its genus with the noun modifier unexposed. (Of (sk_vessel $x) mire_essence) uses the surface preposition entity-attached, which is the licensed open-class oblique shape even though the construction itself is unaddressed.

fields.sentence: Good threads yield a full vessel.
parse: (: threads_yield (Implication (And (Member $x thread) (Member $x good)) (And (Member (sk_yield $x) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $x) $x) (Patient (sk_yield $x) (sk_vessel $x)) (Member (sk_vessel $x) vessel) (Member (sk_vessel $x) full))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: The adjectivally-restricted bare-plural subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route with 'good' as a premise conjunct on the instance variable, and the indefinite object is a dependent Skolem function (sk_vessel $x) with its typing and 'full' kept inside the conclusion; bare-generic 0.9/0.9 and no QuantifierPhrase are both right.

fields.sentence: Poor threads yield a thin slick.
parse: (: poor_thread_yield_rule (Implication (And (Member $x thread) (Member $x poor)) (And (Member (sk_yield $x) yield) (Agent (sk_yield $x) $x) (Patient (sk_yield $x) (sk_slick $x)) (Member (sk_slick $x) slick) (Member (sk_slick $x) thin))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: The adjectivally-restricted bare-plural subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route with "poor" as a premise conjunct (never a kind relation), the indefinite object is a dependent Skolem function (sk_slick $x), and yield's created object takes Patient with the inanimate transitive subject staying Agent.

fields.sentence: Hesper dates and labels each vessel.

review.notes: Coordinated VPs translated independently into two distributing rules over (Member $x vessel), each with its own Skolem-function event and its own 'each' QuantifierPhrase companion; universal strength 1.0 at confidence 0.9, the shared named agent as a constant in both conclusions, and Hesper given a Name atom with no invented type atom.

fields.sentence: Hesper carries the vessels to the cellars.

review.notes: Theme for carry, Goal for the spatial "to", group witnesses for both definite plurals, and the absence of any status atom on a bare simple present all match the instruction set; no kind atom is invented for Hesper, whose single Name fact is emitted.

fields.sentence: The cellar shelves are arranged by year and month.

q2_gaps: a predicative past participle in a present-tense copular clause ('the shelves ARE ARRANGED') — the instruction set pulls both ways: the lemmatization rule declares the same participle in 'the worktop was laminated' a VERB taking the base form, while the focus-particle examples parse 'is heated' / 'is insulated' as adjectival states (reified state + Experiencer + flat atom), so the adjective-vs-passive-event routing here is undetermined

a NON-AGENTIVE 'by'-phrase ('arranged by year and month' = the sorting criterion) — the passive rule states unconditionally that a by-phrase takes the role the active subject would have had (Agent), with no carve-out for a by-phrase naming a criterion or basis rather than the demoted agent
review.notes: Given the adjectival-state route the parse is internally correct: definite plural -> group witness, compound genus with the noun modifier unexposed, PP complement triggering state reification with the flat dual-emit kept, and the coordinated 'by' object distributed into two obliques. The flat (Member sk_group_1 arranged) survives the no-property-on-a-group-symbol bar because arrangement is genuinely a property of the collection.

fields.sentence: The old vessels stand at the front of the shelves.

q2_gaps: a static position predicate (LocatedIn, or a surface-preposition entity head) predicated of a DEFINITE PLURAL: the instruction set routes descriptive modifiers and copular predicates on a plural through the per-member distribution rule and routes distributive EVENT predicates through group-event-plus-rule, but a bare position clause mints no event, so it never says whether the position rides the group symbol, distributes to members, or both — as parsed, nothing answers 'where are the old vessels?' until a member is individuated

"the front of the shelves" as a spatial region noun: the of-phrase is resolved by the generic part/whole test (PartOf), but the instruction set gives no treatment of region nouns (front/back/top/edge of X) as location anchors
review.notes: Definite plural to GroupOf, 'old' as incidental description distributing per-member rather than fusing, no event minted for the postural 'stand' with no reification trigger, and 'at' routed to LocatedIn all follow the instruction set; rule TVs (1.0 0.9) match the distribution pattern.
